items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: this is the first time I met Lee Young, Prez' brother.

ctx.x: He wasn't a terribly gregarious person, was he?

No you had to know him. You had to know him for him to open up to you. You know,he was a very -- actually he was very shy, every way but musically;he was very outgoing musically. But this was a very good experience. Now, while we were rehearsing Lionel brought his first band to New York, and this is the first time I met Lee Young, Prez' brother. They came down, and let's see, Lee Young, Sir Charles Thompson. What is the bass player's name in -- Vernon Alley and Ray Perry, from Boston, played saxophone and played…
But any way they would all come down to hear us

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: they didn't want John Collins and Charlie Harris and myself -- John Collins was the guitarist... so this is how the reciprocal thing came about. They argued it out... if they would allow us to play

ctx.x: Yeah, I started conducting for him, because after I rehearsed at that time, you know, he saw that we got through in a hurry, and then I started conducting for him. I would conduct from the drums -- the drums always sat right down in front of the band, and I conducted all over the country for him. We -- in '53, also, after I joined him, we went to - and in March of '54 -- we went abroad, you know, and we got to London, we were gonna play the Palladium and they didn't want John Collins and Charlie Harris and myself…
the reciprocal thing came about. They argued it out and argued it out, and so if they would allow us to play, then the States was supposed to take Ted Heath, the next year, right?
